metadata.description: Binance Staked ETH (wBETH) is Binance's custodial liquid staking token. Users deposit ETH into the wBETH contract and Binance forwards it off-chain to its own validators; holders receive wBETH whose exchange rate against ETH ratchets up daily as staking rewards accrue. Aggregate user value is reflected in the wBETH market cap of $8.40B — on-chain ETH held by the protocol contracts is a small fraction of this since deposited ETH is immediately routed to a Binance-controlled hot wallet (`ethReceiver`). All administrative roles (owner, pauser, blacklister, masterMinter, oracle, operator, proxy admin) are EOAs operated by Binance; there is no DAO, timelock, or community signalling, and contracts are upgradeable at any time without delay.

admins.name: Proxy Admin (EOA)
admins.description: Binance-controlled EOA holding the proxy `$admin` slot on both wBETH (`WrapTokenV3ETH`) and the unwrap contract (`UnwrapTokenV1ETH`). Can call `changeAdmin`, `upgradeTo`, and `upgradeToAndCall` to swap implementations or rotate the admin slot at any time, with no timelock and no on-chain delay. Worst case = full implementation replacement, capped at the wBETH market cap ($8.40B) since the new logic could mint unlimited wBETH or block all user exits.

mitigations.label: full-impl-swap
mitigations.description: Worst case: replace impl with one that mints infinite wBETH (devaluing every existing holder) or blocks all transfers/withdraws. Bound = total wBETH supply at risk = totalSupply × price.

admins.name: Operations Owner (EOA)
admins.description: Binance-controlled EOA holding the most powerful on-chain role set. Acts as `owner`, `pauser`, `blacklister`, and `masterMinter` on both `WrapTokenV3ETH` and `UnwrapTokenV1ETH`, plus `owner` of `ExchangeRateUpdater`. Can pause transfers/withdrawals, blacklist individual holders, configure minters with arbitrary mint allowance (effectively unlimited mint), rotate every other admin role (`updatePauser`, `updateBlacklister`, `updateMasterMinter`, `updateOracle`, `updateEthReceiver`, `updateOperator`), and replace the exchange-rate oracle contract. Worst-case impact bounded by the wBETH market cap ($8.40B).

mitigations.label: lock-bound
mitigations.description: pause halts wBETH transfer/mint/burn/deposit/requestWithdrawEth. Bound = total wBETH supply (whose holders cannot exit until unpause).

mitigations.label: per-user freeze
mitigations.description: blacklist sets blacklisted[account]=true; modifier notBlacklisted blocks transfer/mint/burn for the targeted address. Bound = the targeted holder's wBETH balance, never spreads to other users.

mitigations.label: unblock only
mitigations.description: Reverses blacklist; only restores access for previously frozen addresses, never extracts funds.

mitigations.label: mint-devaluation
mitigations.description: Worst case: configureMinter grants infinite allowance to attacker who then mints unlimited wBETH, devaluing every existing holder. Bound = total wBETH supply (and therefore aggregate market cap) at risk of devaluation.

mitigations.label: minter revocation
mitigations.description: Sets minters[minter]=false, minterAllowed[minter]=0. Removes ability to mint; cannot extract or affect existing balances.

mitigations.label: mint-devaluation
mitigations.description: Worst case: configureMinter grants infinite allowance to attacker who then mints unlimited wBETH, devaluing every existing holder. Bound = total wBETH supply (and therefore aggregate market cap) at risk of devaluation.

mitigations.label: mint-devaluation
mitigations.description: Worst case: configureMinter grants infinite allowance to attacker who then mints unlimited wBETH, devaluing every existing holder. Bound = total wBETH supply (and therefore aggregate market cap) at risk of devaluation.

mitigations.label: self-burn only
mitigations.description: burns msg.sender's own balance; cannot affect other users' wBETH.

mitigations.label: oracle-replacement
mitigations.description: Worst case: swap oracle to an attacker-controlled contract that pumps exchangeRate, allowing wBETH holders to redeem inflated ETH (or making protocol insolvent). Bound = total wBETH supply since the entire user base is exposed to exchange-rate manipulation.

mitigations.label: withdraw-lock
mitigations.description: pause halts claimWithdraw; pending withdraw requests cannot be claimed until unpause. Bound = ETH currently held in the contract awaiting allocation/claim.

mitigations.label: per-user freeze
mitigations.description: Blacklisted addresses cannot call claimWithdraw on this contract. Bound = the targeted user's pending withdraw amount.

mitigations.label: unblock only
mitigations.description: Reverses blacklist on the unwrap contract; restores claim ability for previously frozen users.

mitigations.label: no extraction path
mitigations.description: rechargeAddress can only call rechargeFromRechargeAddress (payable-add-only). Changing it grants funding-input rights, not extraction rights.

mitigations.label: caller revocation
mitigations.description: Removes a caller's ability to call updateExchangeRate; cannot extract or affect existing balances.

mitigations.label: rate-limited
mitigations.description: Per-caller allowance/interval gate per-call exchange-rate change. require(exchangeRateChange <= allowances[msg.sender]). The cap value is total wBETH supply since exchange-rate manipulation devalues every holder.

admins.name: Zero Address (Renounced)
admins.description: The `rescuer` field on `WrapTokenV3ETH` is set to address(0), so `rescueERC20` always reverts. The Operations Owner can re-enable it via `updateRescuer` at any time, in which case the rescuer could move any ERC-20 mistakenly held by the contract; in normal operation the wBETH contract holds only ETH, so the practical impact of re-enabling is limited to mistakenly-sent ERC-20s.

mitigations.label: disabled-by-state
mitigations.description: rescuer is set to address(0) — onlyRescuer always reverts. Even if updateRescuer re-enables, only ERC-20s mistakenly sent to the contract are at risk; ETH balance and wBETH supply are untouched.

admins.name: ExchangeRateUpdater (Immutable Contract)
admins.description: Sole permitted caller of `WrapTokenV3ETH.updateExchangeRate`. Itself an immutable contract that enforces a per-caller allowance/interval rate-limit (`configureCaller`) on rate updates. The Operations Owner controls the caller whitelist on this contract, and can also bypass the rate-limit entirely by replacing the oracle pointer via `WrapTokenV3ETH.updateOracle` to point at a fresh contract.

mitigations.label: rate-limited
mitigations.description: Per-caller allowance/interval gate per-call exchange-rate change. require(exchangeRateChange <= allowances[msg.sender]). The cap value is total wBETH supply since exchange-rate manipulation devalues every holder.

admins.name: Operator (EOA)
admins.description: Binance hot key handling day-to-day fund flows. On wBETH it can `supplyEth`, `moveToStakingAddress` (forwards contract ETH to the owner-set `ethReceiver`), and `moveToUnwrapAddress` (system-fixed). On the unwrap contract it can `allocate` pending withdraw requests, `moveToBackAddress` (only the surplus over pending requests, by accounting), `setLockTime` (≥ 2 days, no upper bound — can defer claims indefinitely), and update the `ethStaked` accounting field. On-chain ETH directly under operator control is the contracts' transient ETH balance ($2.23M + $26.68K).

mitigations.label: deposits to self
mitigations.description: Operator sends ETH to the contract; payable function only adds to contract balance, no extraction.

mitigations.label: internal funding only
mitigations.description: Routes contract ETH to UnwrapTokenV1ETH (system-fixed via _UNWRAP_ETH_ADDRESS constant) to fund withdrawals. Cannot extract to arbitrary destinations.

mitigations.label: system-funding
mitigations.description: Only callable by the immutable WBETH_TOKEN_ADDRESS to forward ETH from the wrap contract; payable-add-only, no extraction.

mitigations.label: queue-bookkeeping
mitigations.description: Marks pending withdraw requests as allocated (allowing future claimWithdraw); does not transfer funds.

mitigations.label: claim-DoS via time
mitigations.description: Operator can set lockTime arbitrarily high (require(_newLockTime >= MIN_LOCK_TIME=2 days), no upper bound). Pending withdraw requests must wait triggerTime + lockTime; cannot drain funds, but indefinitely defers user exits.

mitigations.label: metadata-only
mitigations.description: Sets ethStaked field that is only emitted in events; never read by any fund-moving path.

mitigations.label: surplus-only
mitigations.description: require(_amount <= availableAllocateAmount - needEthAmount) — only surplus ETH (after covering all pending withdraw requests) can be moved. Pending requests are protected by accounting.

admins.name: WrapTokenV3ETH (System Caller)
admins.description: The wBETH proxy itself is the only address allowed to call `requestWithdraw` and `moveFromWrapContract` on `UnwrapTokenV1ETH` (gated by an immutable `WBETH_TOKEN_ADDRESS` constant). These are system callbacks invoked when a user calls `requestWithdrawEth`/`moveToUnwrapAddress` on the wrap contract; they create withdraw requests or forward ETH to fund withdrawals and have no extraction path of their own.

mitigations.label: system-callback
mitigations.description: Only callable by the immutable WBETH_TOKEN_ADDRESS (wBETH proxy) when a user calls requestWithdrawEth. Records the withdraw request; no extraction by the caller.

mitigations.label: system-funding
mitigations.description: Only callable by the immutable WBETH_TOKEN_ADDRESS to forward ETH from the wrap contract; payable-add-only, no extraction.

admins.name: Recharge Address (EOA)
admins.description: Binance funding wallet. Can call `rechargeFromRechargeAddress` on the unwrap contract to top up withdrawal liquidity (payable-add-only). Cannot extract funds — granting recharge rights to a different EOA via `setRechargeAddress` (owner-only) shifts only the funding-input identity, not extraction rights.

mitigations.label: operational funding
mitigations.description: rechargeAddress sends ETH into the contract to top up withdrawal liquidity; payable-add-only, no extraction.

funds.name: WrapTokenV3ETH (wBETH)
funds.description: The wBETH ERC-20 itself. `tokenInfo.tokenValue` reflects the aggregate market cap of $8.40B held across all wBETH holders — this is the user value at risk from administrative action (mint dilution, transfer pause, blacklist, exchange-rate manipulation). The contract's own ETH balance ($2.23M) is transient: deposits flow through to the off-chain `ethReceiver` via `moveToStakingAddress`.

funds.name: UnwrapTokenV1ETH
funds.description: Holds $26.68K in ETH allocated against pending user withdraw requests. Funded by `rechargeFromRechargeAddress` (recharge EOA) and `moveFromWrapContract` (wBETH proxy); paid out by user-initiated `claimWithdraw` after `lockTime` (currently 10 days) elapses.
